blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Constitution of India.
It consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President of India.
The Constitution authorizes Parliament to determine the qualifications of members and the manner of their selection.
Members hold office for a term specified by the President in his order and are eligible for reappointment.
Qualifications for members are framed by Parliament (via the Finance Commission Act, 1951), NOT explicitly listed in the Constitution.
Members of the Finance Commission ARE eligible for reappointment.
The Chairman must have experience in public affairs, which distinguishes their qualification from the four technical members.

blocks.content: Qualifications are prescribed under the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
